name: TiDB client-go TiKV transaction protocol ownership
Transaction commit outcome must preserve terminal truth

payload.pattern: an RPC may durably apply before response loss, while an upper layer converts uncertainty into definite success, retry, rollback, or failure

name: Transaction cleanup must preserve lock generation identity

payload.pattern: cleanup proves a rich lock identity but carries a strict subset across a layer and can remove a newer or different lock generation

name: Transaction protocol fallback must preserve atomic ownership

payload.pattern: client-go changes 1PC or Async Commit mode after a nonempty prefix of region prewrites while TiKV retains mode-specific lock state

name: SQL terminal result matches durable transaction status

payload.user_promise: a definite SQL success or failure is coherent with the durable primary status and complete logical row image
payload.p_check: an upper layer interprets an RPC result or transaction-status response
payload.q_claim: the transaction outcome is known strongly enough to publish or retry
payload.forbidden: definite opposite result or duplicate replay after an undetermined commit

name: Cleanup removes only its proven lock generation

payload.user_promise: a delayed rollback or resolver cannot invalidate a newer valid lock or another owner
payload.q_claim: the destructive action still targets that generation at TiKV apply time
payload.forbidden: newer generation removed or poisoned by an older cleanup

name: Protocol fallback preserves one atomic transaction key set

payload.user_promise: 2PC, 1PC, Async Commit, and fallback publish one all-or-none logical outcome
payload.p_check: client and storage layers decide or change commit protocol
payload.q_claim: all accepted prewrites and cleanup owners agree on final mode and key set
payload.forbidden: mixed protocol ownership, partial commit, or divergent status

name: Terminal result plus MVCC transaction truth

payload.claim: client terminal result, durable primary status, and complete fresh-session row image are coherent
payload.red: success with absent or partial data, definite failure with committed data, or duplicate effect after retry
payload.green: one coherent outcome or correctly resolved uncertainty
payload.invalid: no proof whether the server applied before response loss

name: Lock generation survives unrelated delayed cleanup

payload.claim: delayed cleanup removes only the lock generation it proved it owns
payload.red: newer or different-owner lock disappears or cannot commit
payload.green: old-only cleanup removes old lock while newer and different-owner controls commit
payload.invalid: schedule does not prove reacquire or owner change preceded cleanup

name: Atomic key set and coherent protocol truth

payload.claim: all mutation keys resolve to one coherent transaction outcome across protocol selection and fallback
payload.red: partial visibility, mixed status or mode, or duplicate logical effect
payload.green: all keys absent or all keys visible under one outcome
payload.invalid: single-region or single-key setup cannot exercise fallback ownership

name: Transaction RPC response lost after server apply

setup: one primary and at least two secondaries
payload.workload: drop or replace the selected RPC response only after TiKV apply witness
controls: same key set without duplicate-sensitive effect

name: Delayed cleanup races a newer lock generation

setup: hold its rollback or resolve action
reacquire at F2 or transfer key ownership
payload.workload: release delayed F1 cleanup after F2 is observable

name: Protocol fallback after nonempty prewrite prefix

payload.workload: make one region accept prewrite before another response triggers failure or fallback

name: Suppress transaction RPC response after TiKV apply

payload.prohibited: generic timeout with unknown apply altitude

name: Cross-layer transaction fault-altitude matrix

altitudes: A3 after response before local publication
steps: pin transaction identity and key set
observe public result and durable truth
controls: same final database state when applicable

name: TiDB does not replay an undetermined commit in the same session

source_proof: client-go returns ErrResultUndetermined for unresolved primary commit or Async Commit/1PC prewrite RPC outcome
TiDB driver maps it to global ErrResultUndetermined
TiDB server closes the connection instead of sending an ordinary retryable SQL error
payload.retired_direction: same-session TiDB automatic replay duplicates an undetermined commit
payload.remaining_boundary: external application retry after connection loss is an idempotency contract, not automatic TiDB replay

provenance.source: TiDB pkg/server/conn.go and pkg/store/driver/error/error.go plus pinned client-go transaction state machine

rationale: Commit outcome is the first source-analysis family in the cross-layer module.
Lock generation is the second source-analysis family in the cross-layer module.
Mode fallback is the third source-analysis family in the cross-layer module.
The selector identifies paths that may violate terminal and durable truth coherence.
The oracle closes public terminal truth against primary status and fresh data.
The selector identifies identity narrowing before destructive cleanup.
The oracle requires both lock identity and a later correctness consumer.
The selector identifies mixed ownership after protocol fallback.
The oracle requires all-or-none visibility and coherent status.
The schedule distinguishes uncertain response loss from pre-apply failure.
The schedule creates two distinguishable lock generations around delayed cleanup.
The schedule creates a nonempty persisted prefix before fallback.
A2 is the critical ambiguity altitude and needs paired altitude controls.
TiDB closes the connection on an unknown outcome and does not feed it into same-session transaction retry.

name: Shared-lock owner commit forces parent DELETE FK revalidation

payload.source_shape: two child inserts hold compatible shared locks on one parent while a parent DELETE waits after an initially empty child scan

matrix.second_holder_commits: DELETE returns FK error and parent plus committed child remain

payload.holding_guard: the committed shared-lock owner creates a conflict above the waiting statement forUpdateTS; TiDB advances forUpdateTS, rebuilds the executor, and reruns the FK check

provenance.source: TiDB shared_lock_test plus current client-go and TiKV owner paths
provenance.introduced_for: highest-consumer close of multi-owner shared-lock release

name: Pipelined stale broadcast commitTS lacks a severe ordinary TiDB consumer

payload.source_shape: CommitTsExpired retry advances the committer commitTS while pipelined broadcast retains the pre-retry local commitTS
payload.holding_guard: inspected ordinary TiKV consumers reduce the broadcast cache entry to committed-versus-ongoing membership and do not use the stale timestamp as SQL visibility truth
payload.retired_direction: promote the commitTS field mismatch without a durable action or highest-consumer consequence
payload.remaining_scope: TiCDC and backup consumers were not evaluated because they are outside this campaign

provenance.source: pinned client-go pipelined committer and TiKV transaction status cache consumers

name: TiKV async prewrite apply remains ordered by scheduler latches

payload.source_shape: prewrite may respond after Raft commit but before asynchronous apply completes
payload.holding_guard: scheduler latches remain held through apply, preventing a same-key commit from overtaking prewrite apply; post-response apply failure uses process termination rather than a false terminal publication
payload.retired_direction: same-key commit overtakes prewrite apply and produces false success

provenance.source: TiKV prewrite async apply and scheduler latch lifecycle

name: Feature capability baseline before transaction candidate

steps: refresh a cached nightly component or select an exact-SHA binary
record the runtime Git Commit Hash
run an existing feature-specific positive baseline
only then run the candidate matrix
payload.invalid: baseline blocks or runtime commit is unknown

provenance.source: local tiup nightly refresh and realtikvtest capability run
provenance.introduced_for: prevent stale component cache from becoming a false bug signal

rationale: The highest-consumer matrix proves that a remaining shared-lock owner commit forces FK revalidation rather than allowing stale parent deletion.
A candidate schedule is meaningful only after the runtime proves the selected feature is present.

name: Revalidate value-scoped proofs after replacement

payload.candidate: value-scoped proofs intersect post-proof replacements intersect irreversible consumers minus revalidation, monotonic derivation, or fail-closed edges
oracle_gate: record exact accepted value and proof arguments
naturally violate only the proof on the replacement
prove the irreversible consumer receives the replacement
rerun the identical schedule with exact revalidation

provenance.source: TiDB cached-table lease checker, client-go CommitTsExpired retry, and TiKV minCommitTS push

name: Cached-table writer pause overlaps healthy reader cache acquisition

preconditions: primary lock TTL greater than five-second cache WRITE lease
writer-local progress and renewal pause longer than lease
healthy peer read before primary lock expiry
payload.positive_example: roughly 4 MiB write gives about 12s primary lock TTL under current production settings
payload.negative_control: small transaction has about 3s TTL and is rolled back before the cache lease window
payload.highest_consumer: INSERT SELECT persists stale cached value into regular sink

name: Successful cached-table commit must not split cache, source, and durable consumer

required_observations: first primary Commit receives real CommitTsExpired
regular sink durably stores old cached value
payload.red: commit success plus cache/source 0/1 plus source/sink 1/0
payload.green: replacement rejected before second Commit and cache/source both remain 0
payload.anti_oracle: checker call count or internal commitTS mismatch alone
